result.title: SLEM: Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging
result.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale model capacity efficiently by activating only a small subset of experts for each input, while still requiring all parameters to be stored in memory, resulting in substantial memory overhead. Expert merging techniques have recently emerged as a promising compression paradigm that reduces this overhead by consolidating multiple experts into a smaller set. However, existing approaches have two key limitations: (i) direct convex interpolation in parameter space is not generally guaranteed to yield meaningful interpolation of expert functions; and (ii) estimating expert similarity or merging coefficients often relies on calibration data, introducing dependence on the calibration distribution. To address these limitations, we propose Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging (SLEM), a calibration-free expert merging framework that occurs in a structured latent representation of expert weights using a VAE. SLEM groups experts within and across layers based on latent similarities and derives merging coefficients from expert weight spectra. It then performs geometry-aware latent interpolation and decodes the resulting representations into merged expert weights. Compared with existing expert merging methods, SLEM achieves comparable or better performance on general knowledge benchmarks and higher average performance on generation benchmarks involving mathematical reasoning and code generation.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 MoE 专家合并在参数空间直接凸插值缺乏函数意义、且依赖校准数据估计相似度的问题，提出 SLEM：用 VAE 构建专家权重的结构化隐表示，在隐空间按相似度分组并做几何感知插值，再解码回合并后的专家权重。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作研究的是权重隐空间中的相似度度量与几何插值，与 LVR 关注的 latent 相似度受内容、深度、位置等因素影响、以及 latent 状态如何比较与融合的问题可能形成方法线索，可供核查其隐相似度定义是否可迁移到推理状态分析。
